rules: PK-0 asserts the original behaviour of L0, including behaviour that is a defect. A baseline defect stays an original obligation; PK-0 cannot delete or redefine it.
A class-H code is a failure mapping, never an accepted semantic refusal. No case asserts class H (C-12 is optional and not authored).
Nothing is asserted for class X. No case places a foreign fault or violates a documented premise.
C-14 (proposed stronger behaviour) is never a PK-0 pass condition and is not encoded here.
No expectation was weakened to make an unrun test likely to pass. An expectation that needs a run on L0 is RECORD_ON_L0 and fails until a reviewed change records the observed value.

A protection fault can never become an expected code (PK0-RC3). In every case child, after the native runtime was initialized, capi_guard_pages sets SIGSEGV, SIGBUS, SIGILL and SIGFPE to SIG_DFL and checks that disposition immediately before and after the export call; a fault ends the child by its signal and the case fails on the abnormal status. The harness-only negative control HarnessFaultControl (test_capi_characterization.py) checks that mechanism without calling any WORLDLINE export, and runs only inside the admitted launch.

C-06 compares the captured fd 2 byte stream exactly (PK0-RC4). A line list stands for ASCII lines each followed by one LF; a recorded stream that is not such a list is written {"hex": ...}. No replacement decoding is used anywhere.

effect_classes.R0: Pre-capture guard refusal: the refusal code; no foreign read and no foreign write; diagnostic lines where the export emits them (C-06).
effect_classes.R1: Post-capture guard refusal: the refusal code; reads exactly the listed frontier and nothing beyond it; no foreign write.
effect_classes.R2: Element refusal at element k: the refusal code; frontier = everything read before the loop plus elements 1..k (paired elements: both members of pair k, in source order); later elements and arrays unread; no foreign write.
effect_classes.R3: Typed outcome encoded by the code or a typed record: the code and the exact writes in canonical order (none for protocol refusals and for the mixed entry).
effect_classes.S: Normal completion: the code and the exact writes in canonical order.
effect_classes.H: Handled internal exception: the handler code; no foreign byte outside the write set changes; completed writes persist, made in canonical order. Which writes completed, and partial completion of a write in progress, are OPEN (9.6.4). Asserted only through the optional C-12, which PK-0 does not author.

open_items.a: Failure location (inside runtime Big_Integer code, an allocation, or a check), hence which writes have completed when the handler runs. OPEN; never an expectation.
open_items.b: Copy atomicity of a write in progress (record assignment through an access value, a Write_Data loop, or a function result built in place). OPEN; never an expectation.
open_items.c: Native write construction of every successor form (A-COST C19, D-36). OPEN; never an expectation.
open_items.d: Preservation of possible outcomes: the successor adds no class-H outcome on an originally accepted input (C21-d) and removes no defined outcome. OPEN; never an expectation.

items: Foreign-pointer faults: no expectation that a fault becomes 255 or -1, and none that it becomes an Ada exception in a Python-created thread (D-23).

controls.C-01: Every case of class R0, R1, R2 or a no-write R3 path without guard pages asserts that each output window is byte-identical after the call (outputs are pre-filled 0xA5 by the region fill, R13; the lifecycle S5 cases keep their S5 mask bytes) and that no byte of the call's mapping outside the windows changed. Never on H or X.
controls.C-02: U7c R3 cases (typed-refusal zeroing of every ledger output over a 0xA5 pre-fill) and U6 R3 cases (mask written only for No_Change/Removal_Planned; preserved for statuses 0 and 1).
controls.C-03: One case per exercisable guard conjunct (ids *_R0_*, *_R1_*, *_R2_*); unexercisable conjuncts are listed per export with the reason. Refused overlaps: U10/U11 Output against Input, Data and Rows; U14 Output against Input and every input array; U14m metadata rows and captured rows against the descriptor; U15f Output against Input and every array. Accepted overlaps: U3/U5 same buffer, U4 Output inside Input or Arena, U8 Result inside Input, U12 Output inside Input. controls.C-05: Cases *_C05_* (and U15f_C16_*_guard): PROT_NONE pages exactly beyond each refusal's frontier and on absent or unneeded inputs, in a forked child under the fatal-fault policy; asserts a normal exit and the expected code only (R14). U15y_C05_*: PROT_NONE on every context and metadata object beyond each join refusal's frontier ('prefix' where the refusal stops inside a row array), and 'end' on every nonempty object of the Authorized paths.
controls.C-06: test_capi_diagnostics.py with the diagnostic_cases of this record: control codes 0/1/2, double enable, stop without start, the failure latch, and the exact WORLDLINE_NATIVE_DIAGNOSTIC byte stream on fd 2 of a fresh child interpreter, compared byte for byte. controls.C-07: test_capi_layout_identity.py: the source sentinel for every probed unknown kind or field of every staying layout export (capi_layout_baseline.json).
controls.C-11: U15x cases: R0 and R1 refusals of the mixed entry, nested-kind readiness refusals, agent refusals, and the decision path compared with wl_collapse_decide on the same request with both roster flags cleared. U15y cases (PK0-RC1): ready Kind 1 and Kind 2 primary and staged sources built by the S5 producers, a well-formed admitted Agent-origin record and joined contexts; the Authorized decision (code 0) together with wl_collapse_decide on the same request with the ready roster flags (oracle collapse_ready, which must itself give Authorized); an Engine-origin record giving the roster-clear decision (collapse_zeroed); and every reachable join refusal. The zero-roster U15x cases are retained unchanged.
controls.C-12: Optional; not authored in PK-0. Class H is therefore asserted by no case.

controls.C-16: U15f_C16_* cases: finalization Operations 0 and 1 with nonzero Row_Count never read Rows (unwritten rows, and PROT_NONE rows) and give the same outcome as the zero-row request.
